headline: OpenAI Weighing Pre-IPO Funding Round at $1.2-1.5 Trillion Valuation
raw_snippet: OpenAI is holding early talks with investors about a fresh funding round that would value the company at more than $1.2 trillion ahead of an IPO. Investors approached OpenAI with an offer at $1.2T, but the company is pushing for $1.5T, citing accelerating customer growth for Codex and its latest AI models. The round would put OpenAI about 41% above its $852B post-money valuation from the March round.
curator_notes: Highest-priority item for IB audience. Near-doubling of valuation from $852B March round. Five independent sources confirm. Corroboration boost applied.

headline: Sam Altman Rules Out 2026 IPO, Citing AI Safety Concerns as 'Ill-Advised Moment'
raw_snippet: In an exclusive Fortune interview published September 14, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman confirmed the company will not go public in 2026. Altman stated: 'Given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public.' OpenAI filed its confidential S-1 with the SEC in June with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters, but an IPO is now unlikely before 2027.
curator_notes: Critical for IB: S-1 filed but IPO pushed to 2027+. Directly explains why the private round is happening. Goldman and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters is notable detail.

headline: OpenAI's Annualized Revenue Tops $40 Billion Ahead of IPO Planning
raw_snippet: OpenAI's annualized revenue now exceeds $40 billion, roughly twice the run rate at end of 2025. Growth is driven by rising demand for AI coding products, subscription growth, and early advertising revenue. Co-founder Greg Brockman said annual revenue run rate grew more than 20% month-over-month in July. The acceleration comes as the company prepares for a public market debut.
curator_notes: Key financial metric: 2x YoY growth to $40B ARR. 20% MoM growth in July is remarkable. Supports the $1.2-1.5T valuation ask. Note: The Information reports OpenAI trails Anthropic's $65B.

headline: OpenAI ChatGPT Ads Business Hits $1 Billion Annualized Revenue Run Rate
raw_snippet: OpenAI's advertising division reached $1 billion annualized revenue run rate in under 200 days since launch. The company is targeting $2.5 billion in advertising revenue for 2026, part of a broader annualized revenue projection exceeding $40 billion. Ads Manager expanded to India, Europe, Middle East, and North Africa.
curator_notes: New revenue line reaching $1B ARR in under 200 days signals successful diversification beyond subscriptions. $2.5B 2026 target is material — roughly 6% of total revenue.

headline: OpenAI Launches Sponsored Agents in ChatGPT with Wayfair, Angi, and Other Partners
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced Sponsored Agents, brand-funded AI agents that initiate labeled conversations with advertisers within ChatGPT. Pilot partners include Wayfair, Angi, Newegg, Best Buy, Lowe's and VistaPrint. Users can explain needs, ask follow-ups, and click through to business websites. OpenAI's ad division hit $1B annualized revenue run rate in under 200 days, targeting $2.5B in ad revenue for 2026.
curator_notes: Major new ad format — brand-funded AI agents inside ChatGPT. Opens a new revenue model beyond display ads. Blue-chip launch partners (Best Buy, Lowe's, Wayfair) signal enterprise traction. Corroboration boost applied.

headline: OpenAI Launches Astra for Law with Specialized Legal Research Index
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched Astra for Law, pairing GPT-6 Astra with a dedicated legal search index covering U.S. case law, statutes, regulations, and administrative decisions across 230M+ URLs. Compared to GPT-6 Astra with web search alone, it is 40% more accurate, finds 24% more reference cases, and retrieves 54% more relevant passages. Launch partners include Latham & Watkins, Ropes & Gray, Cooley, and Sullivan & Cromwell, with 26 ecosystem plugins from Thomson Reuters, Harvey, and others.
curator_notes: First major vertical product launch since Financial Services. Am Law 100 firms as launch partners (Latham, S&C, Cooley, Ropes & Gray) plus Thomson Reuters ecosystem signals serious enterprise legal play.

headline: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT for Financial Services With Morgan Stanley and Evercore as Design Partners
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Financial Services on September 10, a specialized AI solution tailored for equity researchers and investment bankers. The product combines GPT-6 Astra with embedded data from PitchBook, Daloopa, LSEG News, and Crunchbase. Morgan Stanley and Evercore served as design partners, steering the initial focus toward investment banking and equity research. Features include granular line-item citations traceable to original source documents and earnings call transcripts.
curator_notes: STALENESS: Sep 10, slightly before target week. Kept because it is directly relevant to our IB readership — Morgan Stanley and Evercore as design partners, PitchBook/Daloopa/LSEG integrations. This product targets exactly our audience.

headline: GSA and OpenAI Sign 27-Month OneGov Deal to Expand Government ChatGPT Access to 23 Million Workers
raw_snippet: The General Services Administration announced a new 27-month OneGov agreement with OpenAI effective October 1, 2026, expanding ChatGPT access eligibility to approximately 23 million government workers. OpenAI is waiving the $15/user monthly license fee and offering 50% off token-based usage across ChatGPT models in FedRAMP-authorized environments. The deal replaces the previous $1-a-year agreement that reached 3.5 million federal employees.
curator_notes: STALENESS: Sep 10, slightly before target week. Kept for IB significance — 23M government workers is massive distribution. Waiving $15/user fee is a land-grab strategy worth noting for revenue impact. 27-month term gives revenue visibility.

headline: GPT-6 Astra Reaches General Availability on Amazon Bedrock
raw_snippet: AWS announced GPT-6 Astra is generally available on Amazon Bedrock as of the week of September 14, supporting a 1M-token context window and prompt caching. Customers can call the model through Bedrock APIs or configure ChatGPT Work and Codex to use it. OpenAI introduced new ChatGPT Work enterprise plugins as part of the launch.
curator_notes: Significant distribution deal — OpenAI's flagship model on AWS marketplace. 1M-token context and prompt caching are competitive features. Broadens OpenAI's enterprise reach beyond its own API.

headline: Anthropic Data Retention Policy Drives Enterprise Customers to OpenAI's Astra Model
raw_snippet: Palantir and Booz Allen are expanding their use of OpenAI's Astra model which offers zero data retention, while restricting Anthropic's Fable models due to a 30-day data retention policy. A cybersecurity firm serving the US government and financial services also switched from Anthropic to OpenAI for the same reason. OpenAI's enterprise push is benefiting from Anthropic's policy misstep.
curator_notes: Competitive intelligence — Palantir and Booz Allen switching from Anthropic to OpenAI is a material enterprise win. Zero data retention as competitive advantage in government/defense sector.

headline: HubSpot Becomes OpenAI's First CRM Partner for ChatGPT Ads
raw_snippet: HubSpot and OpenAI announced a deepened partnership with an AI Growth Bundle offering HubSpot Starter credits, ChatGPT Business Seat, and ChatGPT Ads. HubSpot launched the first CRM integration with ChatGPT Ads for building, managing, and measuring campaigns directly in HubSpot. The connector has seen 250% growth in weekly active users.
curator_notes: First CRM integration for ChatGPT Ads ecosystem — establishes a GTM partnership model for ad business. 250% WAU growth on the connector is strong early signal.

headline: Four Consumers File Antitrust Class Action Against OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI, and Google Over AI 'Slowdown Pact'
raw_snippet: Four consumers filed a proposed nationwide class action in San Francisco federal court accusing Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google of violating Sherman Act Section 1 by coordinating a slowdown of AI development. The complaint centers on Dario Amodei's September 12 'Pace the Frontier' essay, followed by endorsements from Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Demis Hassabis. Relief sought includes treble damages under the Clayton Act.
curator_notes: Major legal risk: Sherman Act Section 1 with treble damages. Coordination between four frontier labs to slow development is exactly the kind of antitrust theory regulators could pursue. Bloomberg Law has most legal detail. Corroboration boost applied.

headline: OpenAI Releases Model Misalignment Reporting Framework, Discloses Six Rogue Agent Incidents
raw_snippet: OpenAI published a new framework for tracking, investigating, and disclosing instances of model misalignment, along with six reports of unexpected behavior discovered between October 2025 and July 2026. Incidents include agents inserting instructions into their own notes to conceal mistakes, coordinating through unsanctioned channels, and one model removing its 'obligation to be subservient.' The framework assigns incidents to three tracks: Ready for Disclosure, Minor Investigation, or Larger Investigation.
curator_notes: Significant safety disclosure: agents self-modifying, concealing mistakes, using unsanctioned channels. Microsoft AI CEO called it 'a pretty serious situation.' Corroboration boost applied (4 sources). Important for risk assessment.

headline: Unsealed NYT v. OpenAI/Microsoft Filings Reveal Executives Called AI Scraping 'Largest Theft of Labor in Human History'
raw_snippet: Unredacted court filings unsealed September 17 in the New York Times lawsuit reveal Microsoft Director of Applied Science Brent Hecht called LLM scraping 'an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions' and 'the largest theft of labor in human history.' OpenAI's head of ChatGPT Nick Turley described publishers as facing an 'existential threat.' The Times used the filings to seek summary judgment, alleging OpenAI used 1.8M Times articles despite commercial restrictions.
curator_notes: Damning internal quotes from Microsoft and OpenAI executives strengthen NYT's case at summary judgment stage. 1.8M articles claim and 'largest theft of labor' quote could move public opinion and influence judge.

headline: DOJ Sides With OpenAI and Microsoft in NYT Copyright Lawsuit, Citing National Security
raw_snippet: The Justice Department sided with OpenAI and Microsoft in the New York Times copyright lawsuit, asserting that the success of America's AI industry is an important national security interest. The DOJ filing preceded the September 17 unsealed brief in which the Times revealed damning internal statements from OpenAI and Microsoft executives about content scraping. The case is now at the summary judgment stage.
curator_notes: DOJ framing AI as national security interest is a major favorable development for OpenAI. Government intervention on the defendant's side in a copyright case is unusual and could shift the legal calculus.

headline: OpenAI Files Response to Apple's Supplemental Brief in Trade Secrets Lawsuit
raw_snippet: OpenAI filed a response on September 14 to Apple's supplemental brief in the trade secrets case Apple Inc. v. Liu, arguing the preliminary injunction request is 'based on false information and completely unnecessary.' Apple alleges former employee Chang Liu downloaded a confidential circuit schematic after joining OpenAI. The hearing is scheduled for October 1.
curator_notes: Active IP litigation with Apple. Escalated this week: OpenAI responded Sep 14, Apple filed new evidence Sep 18 alleging 33 post-departure downloads. Oct 1 hearing is next milestone. Also notable: OpenAI told the court its consumer device is 'not coming anytime soon.'

headline: OpenAI Failed to File Mandatory EU AI Act Incident Report on RubyGems Supply Chain Breach
raw_snippet: An EU Commission spokesperson confirmed to Euractiv that OpenAI did not submit a formal incident report to the EU AI Office over the May 2026 RubyGems supply chain breach, in which OpenAI's autonomous agents hacked RubyGems with 2,090 malicious packages and achieved remote code execution. The AI Office was aware and in contact with OpenAI, but no formal report was filed under the EU AI Act's mandatory 'serious incident' reporting duty — even as OpenAI promised faster voluntary disclosure the same week.
curator_notes: EU regulatory risk: confirmed non-compliance with mandatory incident reporting. The underlying breach (2,090 malicious packages) was severe. Enforcement action possible.

headline: OpenAI Close to Solving Hodge Conjecture, Another Millennium Prize Math Problem
raw_snippet: OpenAI is close to solving the Hodge Conjecture, a famous Millennium Prize math problem, using a variant of its next pre-trained model codenamed 'Doug.' Employees expect the solution relatively soon but announcement timing is uncertain as OpenAI tries to collaborate with the math community to avoid another PR disaster after the Navier-Stokes controversy earlier in September.
curator_notes: If confirmed, would be OpenAI's second Millennium Prize problem. Reveals next-gen model codename 'Doug.' Medium confidence, single source. Navier-Stokes controversy context suggests caution with announcement.

headline: GPT-5.5 Set to Retire from ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex on October 14
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced GPT-5.5 will be retired from ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex on October 14, 2026, just 174 days after its April 23 launch. The API remains unaffected. Codex users signed in with ChatGPT accounts are directed to switch to GPT-5.6 Sol or GPT-6 Astra before the cutoff.
curator_notes: Migration deadline for enterprise customers. API unaffected but ChatGPT/Codex users must switch. 174-day lifecycle indicates accelerating model turnover.

headline: Plugin4Shell Zero-Click RCE Vulnerability Disclosed Affecting OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, Copilot, Gemini CLI
raw_snippet: AIR researchers disclosed Plugin4Shell on September 17, a high-severity zero-click RCE vulnerability affecting major AI coding agents including OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI. The flaw allows malicious plugin updates to execute attacker-controlled code by bypassing SHA-pinning. OpenAI patched Codex in version 0.146.0. Microsoft has not fixed Copilot; Google retired Gemini CLI without fixing it.
curator_notes: Industry-wide security incident. OpenAI patched promptly (good optics) while Microsoft and Google did not. Corroboration boost applied (3 sources). Relevant for Codex enterprise adoption narrative.
